claim: The new CI env `AOE_E2E_WORKERS: '1'` never reaches the harness, so each CI shard still starts three servers and three workers. The PR says CI keeps one worker per shard, and that is not true.
evidence: `make test-e2e` (make/heavy.mk:66-67) runs through SLOT_RUN, a `docker run` that forwards only HEAVY_ENV (Makefile:28) and SLOT_ENV (make/heavy.mk:5). Neither list contains AOE_E2E_WORKERS, though SLOT_ENV does carry AOE_E2E_SHARD. Inside that container, test-e2e-steps (make/heavy.mk:71) starts a second `docker run` with only `-e AOE_ASSET_PACK -e AOE_E2E_SHARD`. `docker run` does not pass on host variables unless `-e` names them, so `std::env::var("AOE_E2E_WORKERS")` in crates/harness/src/e2e/servers.rs:31 reads nothing and `select` returns DEFAULT_WORKERS = 3 (servers.rs:20, 38-39). As a result, every shard on the 4-core runner still runs three servers per shard, the same setup that timed out the heavy specs in #457. The fix is to add `-e AOE_E2E_WORKERS` to SLOT_ENV and to the test-e2e-steps `docker run`. The docs sentence added at docs/testing.md:136 ("CI sets it to 1") is false for the same reason.
